title: A sound in the dark
hookLine: an empty chariot comes home, and an old king finally tells a secret he has carried his whole life
tomorrow: what does the prince do at the hut?
last: DHARMA KEPT, THE FOREST IS HOME.

cards: Sumantra drives back into Ayodhya alone. The horses hang their heads. People look past him into the empty chariot, and then the wailing starts.
He gives the king Rama's messages, one by one, and Dasharatha sinks deeper into grief. That night, lying beside Kausalya, unable to sleep, he starts to talk. Not about Rama.
About himself, long ago, when he was young and very good with a bow.

teach.h: WHAT YOU DO, YOU EAT LATER.
teach.b: He begins with a saying: whatever a person does, good or bad, they eat its fruit later.
That's karma, one of Hinduism's biggest ideas: every action is a seed, and its fruit comes back to the one who planted it. Then he tells Kausalya what he has never told her.
As a young prince, before their marriage, he was well-known for one skill. He could hit a target he couldn't see, just by its sound.

The Sanskrit word for an archer like that is shabdavedhi, one who pierces by sound. One rainy season, he went out at night along the Sarayu, hoping to catch an elephant coming down to drink. It was dark.

He heard a deep gurgling at the water's edge, was sure it was an elephant, fitted an arrow, aimed at the sound, and let go. From the water came a human cry, and a question. Who would shoot at someone like me?
I live in the forest, I harm no one, I only came for water. The prince ran to the bank.

teach.h: A WATER POT, AND A YOUNG ASCETIC.
teach.b: Half in the river lay a young ascetic with matted hair, an arrow in his chest, and beside him a water pot, the thing that had made the sound. Notice what the old king is doing. He doesn't blame chance for his grief.
In the teaching of karma, what comes back isn't random; it grows from what was done, sometimes long after. A skill he was proud of, a guess in the dark, a shot that can't be called back.
Tonight, with his son gone, Dasharatha believes the fruit has come.

how: Ramayana reciters often tell Dasharatha's confession as its own episode, and later tellings know the young man as Shravan Kumar, in a children's story about care for parents.

o: a warrior who fights only by the light of day
an archer who can hit a target by its sound alone
a hunter who tracks animals by their footprints

games.q: the shot in the dark — tap the pairs.
p: what you do comes back as its fruit
one who shoots at a sound

s: Dasharatha tells this story to Kausalya after Rama leaves
with Sumantra back and the chariot empty, he confesses it at night.
the prince knew a person was at the river
he heard a deep gurgling and was sure it was an elephant drinking.
Dasharatha blames chance for his grief
he opens with a saying about deeds: good or bad, a person eats the fruit of what they do.

games.q: a friend says karma is just the universe getting revenge. what does Dasharatha's saying suggest?
o: whatever you do, good or bad, comes back to you as its fruit.
only bad deeds count; good ones are forgotten.
it's random luck with a spiritual name.
games.why: he opens his confession with it: good or bad, a person eats the fruit of what they do. not revenge, a seed growing.

practice: Close your eyes, or rest them low, and just listen. Notice how fast your mind names each sound, a car, a fan, a voice in the next room, and how fast it wants to act on the name. Let the label go and hear the sound itself.
Many teachers say this small gap, before you act, is where the seed of karma is chosen.

wordCard.voice: Shabdavedhi, one who pierces a target by sound alone. Tonight the old king begins his confession: a shot at a sound in the dark, and a young ascetic at the river.

orig.note: Sanskrit śabdavedhī: śabda (sound) + vedhin (piercing). an archer who hits what he only hears.

carryVoice: Your line: every act bears its fruit. The old king's confession has only begun. See you tomorrow.
